canonical_data: per-run trajectories, screenshots, scripts, and logs written to a local workspace, which the project treats as the state rather than the browser session
current_repo_note: Renamed from microsoft/Webwright on 2026-10-03; the old name redirects here, and existing webwright commands and imports still work.
strengths: Treats the local workspace of code and logs as the state and the browser as disposable, so each solved task leaves a re-runnable Playwright script behind
Every run writes trajectories and screenshots to disk, and an optional Skill Factory distils solved tasks into reusable scripts that rerun without a model
Covers browser and desktop in one tool and ships as a Claude Code or Codex plugin as well as a command line
weaknesses: The benchmark results in the README are the authors' own and several depend on models the README names as the best case
Desktop mode needs Docker, an Ubuntu virtual machine, and gated official task and asset snapshots, which narrows who can run it
The project is six months old, was renamed days before this review, and the desktop runtime is a separately licensed import
why_it_matters: A Microsoft Research harness that argues a terminal-equipped coding model beats step-by-step GUI agents, with published run artifacts to inspect.
